findings.title: Test cleanup removes IDP with literal alias "alias" instead of the created alias
findings.body: In testCacheIDPForLogin, after creating each IDP the cleanup is registered as `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` — the string literal "alias" is used instead of the variable `alias` ("idp-alias-" + i). The cleanup therefore targets a non-existent resource, so none of the 21 IDPs created by the test are ever removed. Consequences: leaked identity providers accumulate in the test realm across test methods (the same test class runs other tests against the same realm), which can break subsequent assertions that count providers, and the cleanup call itself may throw a 404 when executed. The same bug exists at line 425 for the "idp-alias-20" provider. The fix is `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get(alias)::remove);`.

findings.title: registerIDPInvalidation NPEs when the IDP model is null (remove of unknown/nonexistent alias)
findings.body: In remove(), `storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` can be null when no IDP with that alias exists; the code then unconditionally calls `registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp)` (null-safe via the Objects::nonNull predicate), but the pre-existing `registerIDPInvalidation(storedIdp)` path at line 103 dereferences it (`idp.getInternalId()`), throwing a NullPointerException on remove of an unknown alias. While the null-deref itself predates this PR for the invalid-cache branch, the change now also makes the delegate lookup happen on every remove, so any caller removing a nonexistent alias hits it. A null guard in registerIDPInvalidation (or before calling it) is needed.

findings.title: getForLogin cache hit can return IDPs whose organization-aware enabled state differs from the cached list
findings.body: The cached getForLogin result stores only internal IDs and re-fetches each IDP via session.identityProviders().getById(id), which returns the organization-aware wrapper. For an IDP linked to an organization that has since been disabled, the cached login list still contains it and only the consumer-side isEnabled() re-check (added in OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean) filters it out. Any other caller of getForLogin that does not re-check isEnabled (the SPI contract says results are "suitable for being displayed in the login pages") will get disabled-org brokers from the cache. Disabling/removing an organization does not invalidate the cacheKeyForLogin entries, only IDP CRUD does. At minimum the contract should be documented, or the org disablement path should invalidate the login caches.
